page: Microsoft Azure FX48-24ms_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-dense server instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz, configured with 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs via hyper-threading. The CPU architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. The instance is provisioned with 1008.0 GB of system memory, providing 42.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It includes no local storage, relying on attached storage solutions, and contains zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded capability driven by the 4.2 GHz clock speed. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2356.0, placing it in the top tier of evaluated systems, alongside top-tier text processing and small-model LLM text generation rates of 336.04 tokens per second. Memory throughput is also strong in large-block transfers, reaching 187.78 GB/sec read and 120.35 GB/sec write speeds. Conversely, multi-core metrics such as PassMark CPU and stress-ng multi-core fall into the median category, consistent with its 24-vCPU allocation compared to higher-core alternatives.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers an advantageous ratio of memory to compute cores. By bundling over a terabyte of RAM with 24 vCPUs, it enables organizations to support memory-heavy workloads without incurring the software licensing fees associated with 48-core or 96-core systems. The absence of local NVMe storage requires external disk allocation, which represents an architectural consideration for storage I/O design.

The FX48-24ms_v2 is best suited for workloads requiring massive memory footprints paired with high single-core execution speed. Primary workload fits include in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, large-scale software compilation, and CPU-based matrix inference operations leveraging AMX instruction sets.
